newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie's Hannes committed for trial.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie's Hannes committed for trial.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd executive director Simon Hannes was committed for trial on Tuesday on charges of breaching financial transaction reporting laws.

Magistrate Pat O'Shane said in New South Wales local court that Hannes, who was also charged with insider trading, must appear in court on July 4 to make a plea on the financial transaction charges. Hannes' lawyers have indicated he would plead not guilty to financial transactions charges, but have not said how he would plead on the insider trading charges.
The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said it did not expect Hannes to go to trial within the next year.

Hannes, an executive in Macquarie's corporate advisory section, has been charged with insider trading after he allegedly bought A$2.00 TNT Ltd call options in the name of Mark Booth before the successful A$2.45 a share takeover bid for TNT by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
He is also charged with trying to conceal transactions linked to the options trades which, it is alleged, made Booth/Hannes a notional profit of more than A$2 million.
Macquarie advised TNT on the takeover but Hannes was not involved with the TNT account as he was on extended leave at the time.
Hannes is due to appear in court again on June 30 for a hearing on the insider trading charges.
Hannes is alleged to have known about the impending KPN takeover bid for TNT at the time he bought the shares in the name of Mark Booth.
The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) allege Hannes used his magnetic access key to enter Macquarie's Corporate Finance area at night six times in August and September last year.
The takeover was announced on October 2.
The area he entered had documents relating to the TNT takeover that were not locked away, it is alleged.
The ASC said Hannes told them in January that he had entered into an investment syndicate with a "Mr X" investing in the name of his sister Mignon Booth.
Hannes told the ASC he knew Macquarie was doing work for TNT and that TNT shares were on an embargoed list for trade by Macquarie employees.

Hannes told the ASC he had found out "Mr X" had bought the TNT options and had told "Mr X" to reverse the transactions, but this was not done before the call options were bought and the takeover announced.

The ASC has alleged it believed "Mr X" was fictitious and that Hannes had bought the call options in the name of M. Booth knowing he would breach financial transaction reporting requirements and insider trading rules.
